latin-heading.purpose: Headings and UI text for English content. Tight, standard Latin headline tracking.

rtl-heading.purpose: Headings for Arabic and Kurdish content. Looser leading and neutral tracking because both scripts run taller and more connected than Latin Gotham.

shadows.name: mobile-nav-panel
shadows.purpose: The one deliberate exception to the no-shadow rule: the mobile nav sheet genuinely floats over the page content.

shadows.name: timeline-node-ring
shadows.purpose: A solid ring (not a blurred drop shadow) that separates the About page's gold timeline node from the rule it sits on.

motion.name: reveal-on-scroll
motion.purpose: Content registers to a struck datum line as it enters the viewport. Only active when JS has run and the visitor has not requested reduced motion; no-JS, failed hydration, and reduced-motion all resolve to the fully rendered page.

motion.name: button-hover
motion.value: 180ms, transition: color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow, transform
motion.purpose: Hover reads as acknowledgement, not hesitation — named properties only, never transition-all, so the focus ring is never animated into view.

narrative.overview: A flat, restrained, credibility-first B2B industrial site. No drop shadows, no gradients beyond the navy overlay on hero photos, no more than one accent color doing work at a time (gold). Every design decision should read as "established engineering firm," not "startup" or "agency portfolio." The audience is industrial B2B procurement, not consumer or portfolio viewers, so credibility and restraint outrank expression at every decision point.
keyCharacteristics: Four-color system only: navy, cream, lavender, gold — no exceptions without a conscious edit
Flat by default: 1px lavender borders instead of box-shadow, with two named, deliberate exceptions
One script, one type family per document: Gotham (Latin), Somar (Arabic), Ping (Kurdish Sorani), never mixed
Gold is the only accent color and is reserved for eyebrows, checkmarks, badges, hover states, and CTAs

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only "pop" color on the site. If a new component needs to draw attention, reach for gold — not a new color. Navy and lavender are structural (backgrounds/text), not accents.

rules.name: The One Font Family Per Script Rule
rules.body: One type family is active per document, selected by the dir/lang attributes the layout sets from the route. Never mixed within a single language's content.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow. Cards use a 1px lavender border for definition; hover is a small lift plus a border-color change to gold. There are deliberately no shadow tokens in the theme so reaching for one takes a conscious edit. The only exceptions are the mobile nav panel, which genuinely floats over the page, and the timeline node's ring, which is a ring, not a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Explicit Tone Rule
rules.body: Colour on a dark ground is never inherited implicitly. Eyebrow, Checklist, Section, CtaBand, and PageHero each take an explicit tone/dark choice at the call site — there is no cascade to audit, which is exactly why a missed tone stays a review checklist item.

dos: Do reach for gold when a new component needs to draw attention, never a new color.
Do pass tone="light" to Eyebrow or Checklist whenever it sits on a navy ground.
Do use logical properties (ps-/pe-, ms-/me-, start-/end-, border-s/border-e) instead of left/right, so RTL flips correctly.
Do keep each language on its own URL and its own document (/en/, /ar/, /ku/) rather than toggling markup with a CSS class.
donts: Don't reintroduce the teal and coral accent colors from the official brand sheet — Mustafa deliberately dropped them in the 2026-07-24 redesign.
Don't add a box-shadow outside the two named exceptions (mobile nav panel, timeline node ring).
Don't mix Gotham with Somar or Ping within a single language's content.
Don't use physical left/right utilities in RTL-sensitive markup; use the logical equivalents.
